req.title: Show index page
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET / with an HTML page listing all posts ordered by created descending.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that the index page should list all posts in descending order of creation. Tests are designed to verify this functionality, including handling of valid, boundary, and invalid scenarios.

tests.name: test_show_index_page_positive
preconditions: Database is initialized with pre-loaded data.
actions: Send a GET request to the '/' endpoint.
expected: Response contains HTML with post titles in descending order of creation.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

# Initialize the database
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'Heacon signal pulse' in r.data  # Most recent post
assert b'Pulse ember signal' in r.data  # Oldest post

tests.name: test_show_index_page_boundary
preconditions: Database is initialized with pre-loaded data.
actions: Send a GET request to the '/' endpoint.
expected: Response contains HTML with exactly 20 post titles.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

# Initialize the database
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert r.data.count(b'<h2>') == 20  # Assuming each post title is wrapped in <h2>
